verses.commentary: The attacker (mephits, scatterer or shatterer) advances against Nineveh. Ironic commands: guard the fortress, watch the road, brace yourself, marshal your strength! None of it will help. Defense against God is futile.

The Lord restores Jacob's splendor like Israel's. The divided kingdoms reunited in dignity. Though destroyers wasted them and ruined their vines, restoration comes. Assyria destroyed; Israel is rebuilt.

The attackers described. Shields red (with blood or paint or copper), warriors in scarlet. Chariots flash metal on the day they are readied. Spears of juniper brandished. Military spectacle, terrifying and beautiful. The Medo Babylonian army approaches.
Chariots storm through streets, rush through squares. They look like torches, dart like lightning. Speed and fire imagery. The siege moves from countryside to city center. War enters Nineveh itself.

Nineveh summons elite troops, but they stumble. Rushing to defend walls, setting up shields (or protective siege coverings). Panic and disorder. The disciplined Assyrian army cannot coordinate defense. Pride precedes the fall.
River gates opened, palace collapses. The Tigris and Khosr rivers flood. Walls soften and breach. The city's greatest defense becomes its destruction. What protected now destroys.

It is decreed (the word hutstsab means 'it is fixed' or may refer to a queen). Nineveh exiled and carried away. Slave women moan like doves, beat their breasts. The mistress of nations becomes a slave. Role reversal complete.
Nineveh like a pool draining away. Water as metaphor for population and power. 'Stop! Stop!' they cry, but no one turns back. Flight cannot be halted. The exodus from the city is irreversible.
Plunder silver! Plunder gold! Invaders called to loot. Supply endless, wealth from countless treasures. Assyria had accumulated spoils from centuries of conquest. Now others take what Assyria took.

Pillaged, plundered, stripped! Three synonyms cascade. Hearts melt, knees buckle, bodies shake, faces pale. Physical symptoms of terror. The hunters become the hunted. The terrorizers experience terror.
Where is the lion's den? Nineveh called itself a lion. Kings boasted of lion hunts. Where lions and cubs lived unafraid. But where is it now? The rhetorical question mocks. The lion's lair is empty.

The lion killed for cubs, strangled prey for mates, filled dens with the kill. Description of Assyrian predation. They fed their empire by devouring others. Wealth accumulated through violence. Now the predator becomes prey.

'I am against you' declares the Lord of hosts. The most terrifying words possible. Divine opposition sealed. Chariots burned to smoke, young lions devoured by sword. No prey left, messengers silenced. Assyrian heralds demanding tribute will never speak again. Empire ends in smoke and silence.
